title: LegionCapitalRaise.cancel() capitalToReturn does not account for fees already sent out - insufficient funds to refund all investors after cancel
matched_csv_issue: Bidders might fail to withdraw their unused funds after the auction was finalized because the contract does not have enough balance [Size (2022-11)]
description: LegionCapitalRaise.withdrawRaisedCapital() sets totalCapitalWithdrawn = totalCapitalRaised (line 247), but the actual transfer to the project is (totalCapitalRaised - legionFee - referrerFee), while fees are already sent to fee receivers outside the contract. When cancel() is later called (line 285), capitalToReturn = totalCapitalWithdrawn = totalCapitalRaised, and the contract expects the project to return the full totalCapitalRaised. However, if the project only returns what it received (totalCapitalRaised - legionFee - referrerFee), the contract balance is short by (legionFee + referrerFee), causing withdrawInvestedCapitalIfCanceled() calls for the last investors to fail with insufficient balance.

title: LegionCapitalRaise._verifyRefundPeriodIsOver() treats refundEndTime == 0 (before end() is called) as period-is-over, creating dual-pass state inconsistency
matched_csv_issue: Check finalized state with a.data.lowestQuote == type(uint128).max makes fund loss [Size (2022-11)]
description: LegionCapitalRaise._verifyRefundPeriodIsOver() at line 662 uses: if (refundEndTime > 0 && block.timestamp < refundEndTime) revert. When refundEndTime == 0 (end() has not been called), the check silently passes, treating the state as if the refund period is already over. Similarly _verifyRefundPeriodIsNotOver() at line 671 also passes when refundEndTime == 0. Before end() is called, both guards can pass simultaneously depending on context, creating a logical inconsistency that could be exploited if future code paths rely solely on refund period guards without the whenRaiseHasEnded backstop.

title: publishSaleResults() uses caller-supplied askTokenDecimals for totalCapitalRaised calculation; incorrect value causes over-reporting of capital raised and corrupts refund accounting
matched_csv_issue: user fund loss or lock in claim() of the WithdrawProxy because code uses asset decimal instead of 1e18 for calculating transferAmount [Astaria (2023-01)]
description: LegionFixedPriceSale.publishSaleResults() at line 143 computes totalCapitalRaised = (tokensAllocated * tokenPrice) / (10 ** askTokenDecimals), where askTokenDecimals is a uint8 supplied by the Legion bouncer as calldata. If an incorrect decimal value is passed (e.g., 6 instead of 18), totalCapitalRaised is inflated by up to 10^12, allowing the project to withdraw far more bidToken than was actually raised. The acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot set in the same call determines investor refund eligibility; a mismatched decimal therefore corrupts both capital accounting and excess capital refunds.

title: Fee calculation in withdrawRaisedCapital() uses integer division rounding-down, allowing project to receive slightly more than intended at the expense of fee receivers
matched_csv_issue: refund() for ETHCrowdfund may fail for the final user due to rounding discrepancies [Party (2023-04)]
description: LegionAbstractSale.withdrawRaisedCapital() at lines 224-229 computes legionFee = (legionFeeOnCapitalRaisedBps * totalCapitalRaised) / Constants.BASIS_POINTS_DENOMINATOR with Solidity integer truncation. The project receives (totalCapitalRaised - floor(legionFee) - floor(referrerFee)), which is slightly more than intended. The same rounding issue exists in LegionCapitalRaise.withdrawRaisedCapital() at lines 253-258. For tokens with small decimals (e.g., 6-decimal USDC with small raise amounts), rounding errors become proportionally significant and accumulate over many sales.

title: LegionAbstractSale.cancel() callable during refund period causes accounting mismatch: investors who already called refund() cannot use withdrawInvestedCapitalIfCanceled()
matched_csv_issue: A malicious seller can cancel the auction after finalization [Size (2022-11)]
description: LegionAbstractSale.cancel() at line 603 requires only whenSaleResultsNotPublished and whenSaleNotCanceled with no restriction on refund period. If project admin calls cancel() while refund period is active and some investors have already called refund() (setting investedCapital=0 and hasRefunded=true), those investors cannot call withdrawInvestedCapitalIfCanceled() because _verifyHasNotRefunded() reverts at line 453. While investors already received their funds via refund(), the totalCapitalInvested accounting is decremented before cancel, creating state inconsistency where the contract treats the raise as canceled with a different totalCapitalInvested than expected.

title: supplyTokens() lacks whenRefundPeriodIsOver guard, allowing project to supply ask tokens during refund period and creating state ordering complexity
matched_csv_issue: Investors in an ILOPool can lose out on their share of LP position Fees earned from Uniswap V3 [Vultisig (2024-06)]
description: LegionAbstractSale.supplyTokens() at line 372 only requires onlyProject, whenNotPaused, whenSaleNotCanceled, and whenTokensNotSupplied - no whenRefundPeriodIsOver. A project admin can supply tokens during the refund period, setting tokensSupplied=true and transferring ask tokens into the contract while investors can still refund. Although claimTokenAllocation() correctly requires whenRefundPeriodIsOver, this creates a window where tokensSupplied=true but investors can still exit. Ask tokens accumulate in the contract while investor capital may be refunded, and the project cannot withdraw until all conditions are met, potentially creating a deadlock if refunding investors reduce totalCapitalInvested below the expected totalCapitalRaised threshold.
